# Inferra

> Inferra is the Git-native cloud: a PaaS that builds APIs, web apps and background workers from GitHub pushes with Cloud Native Buildpacks and runs them with managed Postgres, a Redis-compatible Valkey cache and S3 buckets.

Inferra runs builds, servers, HTTPS, patching, restarts, rolling deploys, logs and metrics. Website: https://inferralab.com/. Platform API: https://api.dev.inferralab.dev. Product facts reviewed on 2026-10-10 (dev platform, rc.22).

## Configuration and deployment
- Git pushes deploy source. Each repository is an org, each eligible branch has its own space, and apps are named repository folders.
- Two-file configuration: .inferra/org.yaml version 2 declares apps, branch selections, platform domains, service resources, members, shared env and quotas. Read from the default branch only.
- Branch files define build/run/health/deploy settings, service bindings, env and secret names. Read from that branch's exact pushed commit. Missing files use platform defaults.
- main uses .inferra/main.yaml; feature/* uses .inferra/feature.yaml from each matched branch; literal feature/special uses .inferra/feature/special.yaml. Prefixless patterns use .inferra/branch.yaml. Exact matches win, then longest pattern and lexical order.
- Version 1 files still work. inferra init currently writes v1; write the two v2 files by hand. Workflow-only generation supports v2 branch lists and patterns.
- Buildpacks, no Dockerfile: Node.js, Python, Go, Java, Ruby, PHP, .NET, static sites and Procfile apps. Select run.process: worker for a long-running background worker with no public route. Autoscaling is not active.
- Each branch has independent bound services; unbound declarations do not provision instances. Postgres supports backups and restore. The Redis-compatible cache has no persistent storage, backups or restore. Custom OCI service images use private TCP endpoints and restricted gVisor workloads.
- Env precedence: app > branch > org. Secrets are names in YAML, encrypted values in the dashboard or selected-secret GitHub workflow. GitHub Environments use original branch names, including slashes. Missing values fail the commit check.
- Deleting a branch removes its space asynchronously. Pattern-branch services delete immediately; named branches retain Postgres restore eligibility and bucket data for 7 days.

## Credits pricing
- No plans, subscriptions or app limits. Reserved branch CPU, memory and storage plus metered bandwidth, build minutes and backups cost our AWS cost plus 30%, paid from prepaid credits. Bills cannot exceed the prepaid balance.
- $5 of usage free every month per account, shared across all its repos. A card on file is required; never charged unless the customer buys credits. One free allowance per card.
- Branch quotas live under org.yaml quotas:, keyed by exact branch names or patterns, with cpu, memory and storage. Each matching branch pays for its own quota. Missing entries use platform defaults.
- Free reservations must fit the monthly $5 allowance. Paid credits must cover at least 7 days at a new total; rejected changes leave existing quotas running.
- At $0, new deploys pause immediately. After a 3-day grace period, workloads pause; data is kept for 7 days. Top up to resume. Optional auto top-up is off by default.
- Homepage calculator rates are illustrative, not published live AWS rates.

## Security and MCP
- Every app uses a gVisor sandbox. Each branch has a private network; services accept connections only from bound apps. Public outbound destinations are allowed; private ranges and cloud metadata are blocked.
- Every build is scanned for known vulnerabilities. Secret values are not returned by read APIs.
- The remote MCP server uses Streamable HTTP and the user's personal API token, verified on every request. Revoked tokens fail on the next request. All tools are read-only.
- Clients: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and VS Code. Connection examples use https://<host>/mcp; replace the host with the MCP server address.
- Tools: list_orgs, list_spaces, list_apps, app_status, get_logs, get_metrics, list_deployments, explain_failed_deployment, get_org_yaml, propose_config_change.
- propose_config_change returns advisory validation and a unified diff; it writes nothing. The assistant uses its own repo access to open a reviewable PR. Resource: inferra://docs/org-yaml.
- The CLI inspects and operates apps; it does not deploy source.
